questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.stem: In a study group revision of alternative theories, synthesize Enlightenment alternatives to absolutism.

options.text: Only absolutism was ever proposed as legitimate.
Theocracy was the sole Enlightenment alternative.
Consent, rights, and mixed government offered alternatives.
Anarchy was the only accepted option.

questions.explanation: Alternatives included consent and mixed government. Only absolutism or anarchy misstate options.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: Analyzes a source about contract debate

stimulus.body: Some argued the contract creates absolute sovereign power. Others said it protects natural rights and permits resistance. The debate shaped revolutions.

questions.stem: In a study group revision of contract debate, asks what the source best supports.

options.text: All contract theorists agreed on absolute monarchy.
Contract theory had no influence on political practice.
No one ever linked contract theory to revolutions.
Contract theory was contested between absolutist and rights-based readings.

questions.explanation: The source shows contested readings. Universal absolutism or no revolutionary impact misread it.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.stem: In a study group revision of absolutism judgment, synthesize a balanced assessment of enlightened despotism.

options.text: It modernized states but preserved autocracy and inequality.
Enlightened despotism was purely beneficial with no costs.
It had no achievements or reforms at all.
It created full democracy and equality immediately.

questions.explanation: Enlightened despotism modernized but kept autocracy. Pure benefit or no achievements misstate assessment.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.stem: In a study group revision of divergence, identify an example of divergent paths.

options.text: Both states abolished all government in 1688.
England and France both became identical republics in 1688.
England's constitutional monarchy versus France's absolutism.
France became constitutional while England stayed absolutist.

questions.explanation: England constitutionalized, France stayed absolutist. Identical republics or reversed paths misstate divergence.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.stem: In a study group revision of Enlightenment thought, explain how reason undermined divine right.

answer.exemplar: Reason demanded verifiable justification and consent, exposing divine right as unverifiable assertion and shifting legitimacy to human agreement.

questions.explanation: Reason required verifiable consent. The wrong view says reason supported divine right, reversing the critique.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY

stimulus.body: The king modernized schools and courts, but refused to free serfs or share power. He said reform must strengthen, not weaken, the crown.

questions.stem: In a study group revision of reform limits, asks what the source best supports.

options.text: Reform included freeing serfs and sharing power.
Power sharing was the main goal of reform.
The king rejected all modernization entirely.
Reform was limited to strengthening the crown.

questions.explanation: The source shows reform limited to crown strengthening. Freeing serfs or power sharing misread it.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.stem: In a study group revision of idea diffusion, synthesize the impact of Enlightenment ideas spreading widely.

options.text: Widespread ideas had no effect on any political events.
Ideas remained confined and changed nothing.
Dissemination fueled revolutions, reforms, and new political norms.
Only rulers ever encountered Enlightenment thought.

questions.explanation: Widespread ideas fueled revolutions and reforms. No effect or elite-only misstate impact.
